question.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 13 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 13 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 10 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-12{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}-7{x}_{3}=0 \\ -14{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 9 & -7 & 0 \\ -14 & 10 & -8 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -14 & 10 & -8 & 0 \\ -12 & 9 & -7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-7){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{2}(-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-(\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3})+{x}_{3}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=3,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
